0.original: Having given you due warning, Zero would leave you to your own devices.

24.original: Speak with Zero and have her accompany you.

25.original: Gather information while Zero is accompanying you.

26.original: Accompany Zero to the designated location and then speak with her.

27.original: Accompany Zero to the designated location and then speak with her again.

28.original: Search for Farfarello while Zero is accompanying you.

29.original: Speak with Ciriatto while Zero is accompanying you.

30.original: Speak with Ciriatto again while Zero is accompanying you.

31.original: Speak with Ciriatto yet again while Zero is accompanying you.

48.original: 'Tis said that a person's domain is a reflection of what abides in their heart. If true, this place may offer a glimpse into Zero's past.

49.original: The longer one lives, the more one yearns for peace. I understand why some would sequester themselves here.

50.original: 'Tis quite a gathering of voidsent. I pray one among them has the knowledge we seek.

51.original: Consider yourselves duly warned. If you wish to go among the voidsent here, that is your choice to make.

52.original: All have fled from one master or another. But whether any of those masters in turn served Golbez, I do not know. You must ask them yourselves.

53.original: Most have traveled to your world, so it shouldn't be difficult to communicate.

54.original: We shall go about making inquiries at once. Thank you for your counsel.

55.original: Once we've learned all we can, let us reconvene at yonder plaza.

56.original: You're going too, of course? In which case, I shall accompany you.

57.original: I wish only to observe. Do not expect me to help.

58.original: Then it's settled. I'm ready when you are.

59.original: As you may recall, when a larger voidsent is summoned, only its soul makes the journey to the Source.

60.original: Upon its arrival, it takes possession of a host body. But during that time, what becomes of its actual body here in the Thirteenth?

61.original: The answer to this question may give us valuable insight into cross-rift travel.

62.original: To that end, while asking after Golbez, I shall also see what the voidsent can tell me about their experiences when summoned.

63.original: If a voidsent is too weak to create its own domain, it must join with others for protection.

64.original: Alternately, it might devour them in a bid to become stronger, but in so doing risk losing its sense of self.

66.original: 'Twas in order to strike down the Cloud of Darkness that my sister crossed over into the void.

67.original: What befell her after she vanished into the gate? How did she become Golbez's captive? These things and more, I hope to learn...

68.original: Ready? Then lead the way. I leave it to you to decide with whom you speak.

69.original: Zero is now accompanying you. Keep her at your side in order to proceed with quest objectives.

70.original: You can leave Zero behind by entering a different area, or by speaking with her and selecting the option to part ways.

71.original: If you wish to have Zero accompany you again, return and speak with her at the original location.

76.original: Although this is my domain, I don't make a habit of strolling about. 'Tis a strange feeling...

77.original: Are you sure you wish to part ways with Zero?

78.original: You have other business? Fine. Come and find me at my abode when you've finished.

79.original: Finished tending to your other affairs? Then let us continue on.

82.original: I call this my abode, but spend hardly any time here. I return only for meditation.

83.original: While physical wounds can be healed by replenishing one's aether, you can't preserve your form if you lose sight of yourself.

84.original: Such is the risk inherent in consuming another's soul. It dilutes your sense of self. Alters you inside and out.

85.original: To guard against this, I meditate. Visualize who I am, in a place all my own.

86.original: This is the heart of my domain. Normally it's deserted, but you and yours have drawn everyone out.

87.original: I don't recall this statue, though...

88.original: However it came to be here, I certainly didn't wish for it.

89.original: I thought you were her prey, but they say you're her minions. Which are you?

90.original: Are you really a mortal? I've never seen a mortal before...

91.original: <slurp> I bet you taste good. But I can't eat you, else I'll be eaten too...

92.original: You must be accompanied by Zero and have her at your side in order to proceed with quest objectives.

93.original: Zero has yet to arrive. Be sure she is at your side before attempting to continue.

94.original: To walk around with her like that... You're her minion, then?

95.original: You know I don't take minions. <hex:02080CE905FF04536865FF03486503> has some questions, and I want you to answer them.

96.original: Golbez? I don't know that one. Only Scathach.

97.original: When she led us beyond the veil, I grew scared and fled.

98.original: I've been here since. I don't know anyone else, nor do I wish to. That's all I can tell you.

99.original: Scathach was a powerful voidsent who ruled over a vast domain. That was a long time ago, though, so I doubt she has any connection to Golbez.

100.original: I told you─I don't know anyone else, nor do I wish to. Leave me be.

101.original: You're one of the mortals! Is it true? When you die over there, you <hex:021A020203>really<hex:021A020103> die?

102.original: So it is, so it is! What brings you here, then?

103.original: Ah yes, Golbez. He seeks strong minions to grow his army, so I hear.

104.original: But recently, he stopped doing that. Instead, he devours all.

105.original: Perhaps he's gathered enough fodder and is now intent on bolstering his own strength. A sure sign that he is about to make a move.

106.original: By the way, why haven't you died already? Over there, you can do so any time, no? Don't miss your chance, or you'll end up like us.

107.original: <rumble> Stay away from me... If you don't want to be eaten, stay away...

108.original: Golbez, Golbez... I've heard the name before.

109.original: Ah, I remember! Always speaking of a great crusade. I don't know what that is, but it sounds delicious. <slurp>

110.original: A crusade, you say? From whom did you hear this?

111.original: Farfarello. He was a minion of another minion. Went on and on about the terrible things he saw.

112.original: I see... Perhaps Farfarello can tell us more.

113.original: Why do you want to know about Golbez? Do you have a crusade too?

114.original: Satisfied with what you've learned? Ah─but let's step away before you become too tempting to resist.

115.original: It seems the rumors of Golbez reach even my remote domain.

116.original: Fair to assume he's gathering strength for his crusade─whatever that may be.

117.original: But I must say, I wouldn't have guessed that Farfarello once fought in Golbez's army. It's a miracle he survived serving an archfiend.

118.original: Ah, I suppose I should explain.

119.original: Farfarello is the weakest among us. Constantly in fear of being devoured, he seldom consorts with others.

120.original: The only one he's comfortable with is Ciriatto.

121.original: He's a fellow coward who runs the instant he senses a threat, and won't stop until he's exhausted.

122.original: When their hunger grows too intense, they feed on each other's aether. Such is their relationship.

123.original: But I ramble. You intend to seek out Farfarello, I presume?

124.original: Then I'll come with you. He's less likely to hide that way.

125.original: Farfarello keeps to the fringes of my domain. This way.

127.original: The voidsent here don't answer to a master. They can do as they please.

128.original: But all must answer to the hunger, and seek out prey when they need aether.

129.original: Except Farfarello and Ciriatto, that is─they are content to take from one another. Barring an incident, they dare not venture out.

130.original: When he takes flight, Ciriatto will not seek shelter until he is utterly spent. Farfarello, on the other hand, prefers to hide in the same place. Come.

131.original: Uwaaaaaah! P-Please don't eat me...but I suppose you have to...

132.original: Oh, whatever will I do now? <whimper>

133.original: Ciriatto... This is rather unexpected. Where is Farfarello?

135.original: Farfarello...isn't here anymore. He's...left. Y-Yes, that's right!

136.original: Left? That doesn't sound like him at all.

137.original: W-Well, he's gone, all right? Wh-What more do you want me to say?

138.original: And off he flees, as he is wont to do.

139.original: But something about this doesn't sit well with me...

140.original: What do you make of Ciriatto's behavior?

142.original: He seemed frightened. Perhaps someone had threatened him?

143.original: I don't think he was telling the truth.

144.original: I doubt it. Had he been threatened, we wouldn't have found him in one place.

145.original: No, he would run in circles until he could run no more. That's his nature.

147.original: As he says, Farfarello is gone. But that is quite unusual.

148.original: As is the fact that Ciriatto, who was clearly frightened by something, chose not to flee but instead hid here, where Farfarello usually─

150.original: We must go after Ciriatto. Now.

151.original: I know Farfarello was our quarry, but Ciriatto's behavior troubles me. We must find him.

152.original: I-I don't have time for this... You'd best keep your distance if you know what's good for you!

154.original: Th-There's no time! The wind rises! We must flee!

155.original: The wind rises...? What is he talking about?

157.original: Uwaaah, the wind howls! Louder and louder!

158.original: What's gotten into you? What do you mean, the wind rises?

159.original: When the wind rises, she comes! <hex:021A020203>Barbariccia<hex:021A020103>!

160.original: Barba...riccia? Who in the world is that?

161.original: We must flee, all of us! There's no time!

162.original: I don't sense anything, but he seems convinced.

163.original: It's a dead end beyond. We'll corner him.

164.original: Ahhh, it's too late! The wind is already upon us!

165.original: We're doomed! There's nowhere to run!

167.original: I-I already told you! Barbariccia, the archfiend of wind!

169.original: We will be devoured or forced to serve. To fight in the crusade. But it makes no difference. In the end, all are eaten by her or her enemies.

170.original: I didn't want to fight anymore. That's why I fled and came here!

172.original: I thought it was Farfarello who used to serve an archfiend. Not you.

173.original: Not you, who always ran at the first sign of trouble. You who now speak as though you were Barbariccia's minion. There's only one explanation...

177.original: Indeed, that would account for his uncharacteristic behavior.

178.original: So, is that the way of it? Did you devour Farfarello?

179.original: And not just a portion of his aether, but his entire being.

180.original: Tell me true, Ciriatto. You devoured Farfarello, didn't you?

181.original: And not just a portion of his aether, but his entire being.

183.original: It wasn't only your behavior that felt strange.

184.original: <hex:021A020203>You<hex:021A020103> felt strange. As if there was more than you present.

185.original: Now, I don't believe you would've lost control. More likely it was at Farfarello's behest.

186.original: I can't hide anything from you...

187.original: I admit it. Farfarello didn't leave. I ate him.

188.original: He feared Barbariccia more than anything. Hated the endless fighting.

189.original: So he begged me to devour him, that he would never have to fight again.

190.original: Rather than an eternity of fighting, he chose a moment of pain...

191.original: For all the good it did. I can still hear his voice in my head. He's frightened, so very frightened...

192.original: When you're eaten, your essence is blended with that of your devourer. And though you have no control, your consciousness in part endures.

193.original: Were this a world where the wheel of life and death still turned, the soul wouldn't linger so stubbornly.

194.original: In time, it would return to the great flow.

195.original: But there's no such end here. No escape. All know this. In making his choice, Farfarello must have been desperate indeed.

196.original: And now that desperation has joined with Ciriatto's fear, driving him to act erratically.

197.original: This place will become a battlefield. We don't want to be eaten. Neither me nor Farfarello. But there's nowhere to go! Nowhere!

198.original: Then tell me about Barbariccia. I would know who it is we face.

199.original: It's too late. She's as good as here, and no one can escape her winds! No one!

200.original: What little I learned in your absence did not pertain to the archfiends. That discussion can wait until after we've tended to Barbariccia.

201.original: Just you wait, Barbariccia. I will have answers from you yet...

202.original: I have no intention of demanding anyone's aether until afterwards. Weakening you now would only reduce my chances of getting paid.

203.original: The less time we give the enemy to prepare, the better. If everyone is ready, then let us set forth.

204.original: Indeed. And yet...my heart weighs heavy for those Barbariccia struck down. Were it not for us, she would not have come here.

205.original: Should you require a moment, Zero...

206.original: For what? Barbariccia took what she could. She was wise to strike quickly─as we would be.

207.original: Agreed. This is no time for sentiment. Only the battle matters now.
